title: Working in Philadelphia, Newark and Washington without a cabaret card
summary: McLean played Philadelphia with Reggie Workman and young McCoy Tyner, a battle of the altos, and a Washington club the week of King's speech.

bands.name: Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

blocks.x: Were you conversely going to Philadelphia and doing things? Or going to Detroit and doing things?

Oh yeah. I was going to Philly more than I would be going to Detroit. I went to Detroit with bands. That’s the only time I ever went to Detroit, when I either went with Mingus or with Art or with somebody. But Philly, I used to go down there by myself, because different people would call me down to work. Like Reggie Workman would call me and say, “Jackie, I’ve got a club that wants you to come down. All you got to do is let me get a rhythm section for you.” So he would get young McCoy Tyner. McCoy was only about 18 then. I forgot who was playing drums at that particular time. And Reggie and myself. This guy named Johnny Splawn, who played trumpet in Philly, was – taught Lee. He was on crutches, but he could play. So I got a chance to go down and play with them, and I got a chance to go down there and play with Cee Sharpe and other saxophone players. They would put us together. They had like a battle of the altos on a particular Sunday in a theater. They had some very interesting things going on in Philly.
Between Philly and Jersey, was that – were you able to – I’m going to ask you, was the same thing happening, say, in Newark for you?
Yeah, I went to Newark to play, mostly though with somebody’s band. I have gone over there, done some things with my group. But most of those guys hung out in the city.
I guess where I was going was, did those things make up for your inability to work in clubs in New York?
Yeah, if I got a chance to play in another town, yeah. I didn’t have to worry about a cabaret card or anything like that.
Did that – how far down the East Coast? Were you going to Baltimore? Were you working in Washington? Were those . . . ?

Every once in a while, something would come up. We would be working somewhere in Washington. Like the week that Martin Luther King did his speech at the Lincoln Memorial, I was in a club. I was in the Caverns, when that was open down there.
